issues.title: Transactions not merged when applying rules to existing transactions (transfer double-count)
issues.harvest_why: MONEY+CRDT: applying a rule that turns payees into transfer payees on two existing opposite transactions creates new transfer legs instead of linking the existing ones, so A=-50 and B=+50 instead of -25/+25. The fix is in server/transactions/transfer.ts plus the rule-apply/batch-update path (transactions/index.ts batchUpdateTransactions with runTransfers). It writes transfer_id and tombstones on the transactions table. A sloppy fix can leave orphan legs or one-sided transfer_id.
issues.author: author-agent:issue-1331

issues.title: API transactions-add: a rule that sets a transfer payee creates no counterpart leg
issues.harvest_why: MONEY+CRDT: in api.ts, 'api/transactions-add' defaults to runTransfers=false. After runRules in accounts/sync.ts addTransactions sets a transfer payee, no leg is inserted, so account B's balance never changes. The fix touches transfer creation (transfer.ts) and the API defaults. A wrong fix can create duplicate legs or a leg without a back-link transfer_id.

issues.title: Splitting a transaction that is a transfer to an off-budget account produces unmatched duplicate legs
issues.harvest_why: MONEY+CRDT: in server/transactions/transfer.ts, how split children and the parent carry the transfer payee to an off-budget account, which sometimes adds an extra +3000 to the off-budget ledger. The fix writes transfer_id, parent/child rows and tombstones, and the sum of the children must still equal the parent.

issues.title: API updateTransaction on a sub-transaction clears its category and amount

The fix keeps split integrity (sum of children = parent) in synced transactions writes. Earlier PRs #8132 and #9059 were closed, not merged.

issues.author: author-agent:issue-6682
issues.reason: The natural fix for this issue is entirely in the client, not in packages/loot-core, so loot-core tests cannot express it fairly. I ran a probe on the untouched A variant (since deleted). It created a schedule through 'schedule/create', added per-split rule actions through 'rule-update' (set-split-amount plus `set payee` with options.splitIndex 1 and 2), started the schedules services and posted with 'schedule/post-transaction'. The server already gives each child the payee from its split action: child -2000 got payee p2 and child -3000 got payee p3. So the rule split actions, execActions and postTransactionForSchedule plus runRules already handle per-split payees. The bug is in packages/desktop-client/src/util/schedule-actions.ts. There, createSingleTimeScheduleFromTransaction (convert-to-schedule) writes split actions only for amount, category and notes, never for each split's payee. The fix is to add a `set payee` action per split in that client util. Hidden tests must be loot-core test files (validate_layout), and any server-level test would pass on the untouched variants. A test that fails today would have to check the client's rule-building, which goes against the task's MONEY+CRDT/loot-core purpose. Side observation (not this issue): the posted parent transaction ends up with a null payee (description) even though the schedule's payee condition is set. That might be a separate server-side task if someone files it. No task directory was created. The probe file was removed from work/variants/A, and other agents' untracked files in A and AP were left alone. Natural fix is client-only (desktop-client schedule-actions.ts); loot-core already applies per-split payees.
